ABOUT ME

Curiosity becomes valuable when it is turned into a working system.

I am a STEM student interested in the point where computer science, scientific research, and engineering meet. I enjoy understanding a problem from first principles, testing an idea, and iterating until it becomes useful.

That approach has taken me from programming and robotics to ECG signal analysis, machine-learning pipelines, embedded systems, and technical leadership.

Featured research

BIOMEDICAL AI · 2026

AI-Synchronized ECG System for Early Cardiovascular Risk Analysis

A research prototype combining ECG acquisition, computational feature extraction, machine learning, and real-time monitoring to study cardiac abnormalities and elevated cardiovascular risk.

ECG SIGNAL / SAMPLE VIEWPTB-XL
TemporalMorphologyFrequencyWaveletsEntropyRMS

RESEARCH QUESTION

Can multidomain ECG features support earlier identification of clinically relevant cardiac patterns?

The system uses Kareem’s own modeling pipeline—not a third-party AI API—covering preprocessing, signal segmentation, engineered features, classification, and evaluation.

WHY AI & COMPUTER SCIENCE?

My path was not a straight line into AI. It was a sequence of harder questions.

STEM education taught me to connect disciplines. Programming gave me a way to test ideas. Robotics made those ideas physical. Scientific research taught me to measure, question, and iterate. Biomedical AI brought all of those threads together around problems with genuine human consequence.
